In Progress and Free: Strategy and Research Brief

Why the page works the way it does, and the evidence behind it. Version 1.0, November 2026. Companion to the Content SOP (how we do it) and the Page Development Log (what happened and when).

1. Purpose

This brief explains the strategy for In Progress and Free, sets out the research it rests on, and states what that research can and cannot support. It is written so the owner, a reviewer, or a client can follow the reasoning without reading the full conversation record.

2. Positioning

One line: philosophy, feminism, and freedom of mind, for everyone, in plain language and a calm tone.

What it is not: an expert talking down, a motivation page, a hustle page, or a clinical resource.

Angle: big ideas turned into everyday tools. Most self-growth pages offer encouragement. This page offers ways of thinking and things to try this week.

Voice: calm, honest, and unfinished on purpose. The name says it: in progress and free at the same time.

Look: sky and ocean photography, navy, sky blue, cream, and a peach accent, with a serif display font.

3. Audience

Who: teenagers and young adults, based in the Philippines.

What they are looking for: ideas about who they are, who shaped them, and how to choose for themselves, without lectures.

Where they are: mostly on Facebook and TikTok (see section 6).

Safety: some readers may be struggling. The page includes a Support highlight for the Philippines and avoids diagnosing or giving clinical advice.

4. Goals and how success is measured

GoalMeasure
Educate and raise awarenessSaves and shares of carousels
Encourage empowerment and freedom of mindReplies and messages that describe a change in thinking
Grow organicallyFollowers gained per month; reach to non-followers
Serve as a portfolioA complete, consistent page with documented process

Primary signals: saves and sends. Every post is built to be kept and passed on. Views are tracked but are not the goal, because views alone do not show whether the content helped anyone.

5. Strategy

5.1 Funnel: entertain, educate, invite

  • Entertain the masses (60%): easy-to-share posts, such as photo quotes and short Reels.
  • Educate the interested (30%): the six-slide carousels and weekly summaries.
  • Invite the committed (10%): the Start Here highlight, weekly prompts, and an optional broadcast channel.

No selling. The page earns trust first.

5.2 Growth tactics

  • 80/20 rule: 80% of content in the page’s own formats and pillars, 20% adapted from trends.
  • Stay and send design: each carousel gives the reader a reason to stay through all slides and to pass it on. The last slide asks for a save and a send.
  • Daily engagement: 15 to 20 minutes of genuine comments and replies. No follow-for-follow.
  • Consistent rhythm: carousels on Sunday, Tuesday, and Thursday; photo quotes on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday; a summary on Saturday. Each quote echoes the post before and teases the next, so followers have a reason to come back.

5.3 Platform roles

  • Instagram: the main portfolio and the home of the full grid.
  • TikTok: reach, using carousels and short videos.
  • Facebook: broad Philippines reach and backup. It was first treated as secondary, then raised in importance after the usage data in section 6.

6. Research summary

FindingSourceWhat it supportsLimits
In the Philippines, Facebook is used by about 94.9% of internet users, Messenger 90.6%, YouTube 85%, TikTok 82.2%, Instagram 71.2%.Digital 2026 Philippines, DataReportal, Meltwater (searched Oct 2026)Using Facebook and TikTok as reach platforms, not Instagram aloneSurvey-based national averages, not specific to this niche or age group
Daily time: Facebook about 1 hour 31 minutes, TikTok about 1 hour 30 minutes, Instagram about 34 minutesSame sourcesPrioritizing Facebook and TikTok for time spentSame limits
Instagram now allows five hashtags per postSearched Oct 2026One brand tag plus four topic tagsPlatform rules change
Sends and shares are weighted heavily in ranking, especially for non-followersThird-party summaries of statements by Instagram’s headDesigning for saves and sendsSecondhand; Instagram does not publish exact weights
US teens use YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram heavily, and Facebook far lessPew ResearchGeneral context onlyUS data. It does not describe Filipino teens, so it was not used to set strategy
Metacognition means thinking about one’s own thinkingFlavell (1979), American Psychologist 34The Metacognition carousel’s definitionFoundational paper; check the exact citation before quoting
Change is often nonlinear, with setbacks commonProchaska et al. (1992), stages-of-change modelThe tree-not-ladder message in the Growth carouselDeveloped in smoking-cessation research, so it is scoped to habit change and not to all growth
Mentally detaching from work relates to lower burnoutJob-strain and burnout researchRest content, with careEvidence is mixed. It is not a cure-all, and posts must not diagnose

Rule: every claim in a post needs a source logged in the Research Template. If the evidence is mixed or limited to one setting, the post says so or leaves the claim out.

7. Content system

Pillars: Philosophy of Self; Feminism for Everyone; Fragile but Growing; Actionable Awareness. Thinker spotlights cut across the four.

Topic pipeline: where it came from (conditioning), notice it (self-awareness), question it (metacognition, critical thinking), choose it (values, autonomy, boundaries, identity), sustain it (growth, character, discipline, rest, self-compassion). Each week’s three carousels follow this path so the page builds a clear sequence, not a random list.

Six-slide template: Cover, Define it, Understand it (with a metaphor), Why it matters, In your day, Realization. It makes each idea easy to follow and easy to make.

Thinkers: Beauvoir, bell hooks, Frankl, Freire, Lorde, the Stoics, Kafka, Nietzsche (used critically because of his views on women), Adichie, Sen, Nussbaum, and Arendt.

8. Early results (small sample)

The page has been live for only days. The numbers below are too small to treat as conclusions.

  • Carousels with a one-word cover and a direct question led on TikTok views, reaching 287 for the best post.
  • Static quote posts and the question-of-the-week post trailed, at 9 and 5 views.
  • Followers moved from 3 to 4 while likes rose from 16 to 34.
  • The owner noticed more views when posting at 4 or 5 a.m. This is a lead, not a finding.

9. Risks and safeguards

RiskSafeguard
Readers in distressSupport highlight with Philippine helplines, rechecked monthly. Numbers are from news and directories until verified on official pages.
Over-claiming from researchSource rule in section 6; scope claims to what the study covers
Mental-health content read as diagnosisDescribe signs only. Add a line directing readers to a doctor or counselor.
Gender, legal, and health topicsUse Philippines-specific sources before posting
Misattributed quotesUse only quotes whose origin is clear, or write original lines
Linking the page to a personal accountKeep accounts separate: different email, no tags, no cross-promotion
Burnout from posting too muchKeep to the weekly rhythm. Add Reels only if time allows.

10. Open questions and next tests

  1. Posting time: compare 4 to 5 a.m. against evening over 8 to 10 posts, logging saves and sends with the time posted.
  2. Facebook: does Facebook deserve equal effort, given the usage data? Review after a month of results.
  3. Reels: do voiceover Reels over nature footage add reach, or do carousels carry the page alone?
  4. Conversion: are views turning into followers? Test a clearer reason to follow in the bio.
  5. Research gaps: fill in the Research Template, starting with bell hooks, and verify the helplines on official pages.

10. Research record

Platform use in the Philippines (searched Oct 26 to 27): Facebook 94.9%, Messenger 90.6%, YouTube 85%, TikTok 82.2%, Instagram 71.2% of internet users. Daily time: Facebook about 1 hour 31 minutes, TikTok about 1 hour 30 minutes, Instagram about 34 minutes. Sources: Digital 2026 Philippines, DataReportal, and Meltwater.

Hashtags: Instagram limits posts to five tags (searched Oct 26).

Metacognition: the term comes from Flavell (1979, American Psychologist, 34). Credited on the Metacognition carousel. Confirm before relying on it.

Non-linear change: Prochaska et al. (1992), the stages-of-change model, cited on the Growth carousel. It comes from smoking-cessation research, so the claim is scoped to habit change.

Burnout: psychological detachment from work relates to lower burnout, but evidence is mixed. Posts describe signs only and do not diagnose.

Support highlight (Philippines, last checked October 2026, not yet verified on official pages): the helpline numbers are kept in the working copy and are not published here until they are verified.

In Progress and Free: Brand Kit

Mortal, fragile, and still becoming. Version 1.0, November 2026.

1. Who we are, and who we’re for

Mission: philosophy, feminism, and freedom of mind, for everyone. Big ideas turned into everyday tools, in a calm and honest voice.

Audience: teenagers and young adults in the Philippines, curious about who they are, who shaped them, and how to choose for themselves.

Framework: Notice it. Question it. Choose it. Our own three-step way to think for yourself. It is not a clinical model.

Personality: calm, honest, curious, kind, unfinished on purpose.

We areWe are not
Plain and warmAn expert talking down
Practical, not preachyA hustle or motivation page
Open about what we don’t knowA clinical or medical resource

2. The mark and the name

  • Leave clear space around the mark equal to the width of the peach dot ×4.
  • Minimum size: 48 px for the mark, 160 px wide for the mark with the name.
  • The ring is navy on light backgrounds and cream on dark ones.
  • Don’t: stretch, rotate, or recolor the mark; place it on busy photos without the navy tint; change the italic “and” in the name.

3. Five colors, one calm palette

Navy#0F2A43Backgrounds, headlines on light
Ocean#1F5F8BSecondary background, links
Sky#BFD9EALight background, tags
Cream#F7F3ECPage background, text on dark
Peach#F2B48CAccent on dark, one word at a time
Contrast (WCAG)RatioResult
Cream on Navy13.3:1Passes for all text
Navy on Sky10.0:1Passes for all text
Navy on Cream13.3:1Passes for all text
Cream on Ocean6.2:1Passes for body text
Peach on Navy8.2:1Passes for all text
Peach on Cream1.6:1Do not use for text

Rule of thumb: peach is for dark backgrounds only. On cream or sky, use Ocean for the emphasized word.

4. Two typefaces, one hierarchy

Display: Cormorant Garamond. Quiet, editorial. Headlines, quotes, and the emphasized word in italic. Use SemiBold on busy video.

Labels and small text: Inter. Clear and neutral. Pillar labels in capitals with wide letter-spacing, page counters, and handles.

For 1080 × 1350 postsSizeStyle
Cover word70 to 90 pxCormorant, italic, accent color
Headline44 to 54 pxCormorant, regular
Body30 to 34 pxCormorant, regular
Label15 to 18 pxInter, capitals, letter-spaced

Fallbacks if the fonts are missing: Georgia or a similar serif for display, and Arial for labels.

5. Four formats, one look

6. Sky and sea, with room to breathe

  • Use our own photos and footage of sky, sea, and shore.
  • Keep open sky in the top third, where the text sits.
  • Shoot vertical and hold the phone steady.
  • Add a navy tint (about 40 to 60%) so cream text stays readable.
  • Avoid faces, house numbers, and other private details.
  • Avoid cluttered foregrounds and busy white foam behind text.

7. How we sound

DoDon’t
Short, plain sentencesShame, hustle, or “just try harder”
Offer one idea and one thing to tryDiagnose or give medical advice
Say “you might” and “one way to”Claim more than a source supports
Give a source when we cite researchEnd with a comment question

Caption anatomy:

  1. The idea in one or two sentences.
  2. A teaser for the next post, if it is a quote.
  3. The closing line: Save this for when you need it, and send it to someone who does.
  4. Five hashtags: #inprogressandfree plus four topic tags.

8. Small rules that keep it consistent

Posts

  • Rotate cover colors: Navy, Sky, Cream, Ocean.
  • One emphasized word in italic: peach on dark, ocean on light.
  • Keep text clear of the edges, since the grid crops covers.
  • End carousels with the save/send line.

Stories and video

  • Keep text between the top 15% and bottom 25% of the screen.
  • Place the page name and handle above the bottom 25%.
  • Reels: up to 10 seconds, calm footage, soft ambient sound.
  • Use the logo end card in the last two seconds.

Always

  • Sources checked before posting.
  • No diagnosing; point to a doctor or counselor.
  • Philippines helplines re-checked monthly.
  • Same handle on every platform.

In Progress and Free: Prompt Library

Reusable prompts from the page’s start to its current progress, organized by stage. Version 1.0, November 2026. Owner: Quelene Santiago.

How to use this library

  • These are cleaned-up versions of the requests actually made, not word-for-word copies. Each one is rewritten as a template. Replace anything in [brackets] with your own details.
  • Dates come from the conversation record. Entries from Oct 24 to 26 are exact (Philippine time). Later entries are approximate.
  • Good prompts have four parts: context (who and what), task (what to make), format (how it should look), and constraints (what to avoid). Each prompt below shows all four where they matter.
  • Add the guardrails in section 9 to any prompt that touches research, mental health, or privacy.

Prompt anatomy

Context: [who the page is for and what it is about]. Task: [what you want made]. Format: [size, length, structure]. Constraints: [tone, sources, things to avoid].

1. Discovery and naming (Oct 24)

1.1 Page briefUsed: Oct 24, 13:36

I want to be a digital creator who educates people and raises awareness about [topics]. I want to encourage [values]. My imagery is [theme]. My audience is [who]. I don’t have a name yet. Suggest name ideas, content pillars, and platforms, and ask me what you need to know.

1.2 Name brainstorm from influencesUsed: Oct 24, 13:40 to 13:42

I’m inspired by [thinkers]. My page is about [mission]. Give me [10] name ideas in [two or three] directions, with a one-line reason for each. Avoid names that sound [too academic, too aggressive]. Here are names I already like: [list].

1.3 Themed naming roundUsed: Oct 24, 13:48

Give me names that reflect these ideas: [awareness, protecting the self, freedom in difficult circumstances, peace about mortality]. Keep them short and easy to say. Suggest a possible tagline for the best three.

1.4 Compare a shortlistUsed: Oct 24, 13:44 to 13:54

Compare these names: [list]. For each, tell me the feeling it gives, who it might put off, how easy it is to spell and remember, and what handle variations I could try.

1.5 Decide the name and taglineUsed: Oct 24, 14:02 to 14:08

I like [name] because [reason]. Suggest a tagline that adds [philosophical angle]. Give me three options and tell me which you’d choose and why.

1.6 Logo requestUsed: Oct 24, 14:13 to 14:19

Design a logo for [page name]. Theme: [sky and ocean]. Palette: [colors]. Style: [calm, minimal]. Give me a primary version, a dark version, and a square profile-picture crop.

1.7 Bio optionsUsed: Oct 24, 14:21

Write three bio options for [platform] under [150] characters. Include [tagline] and what people will get. Tone: [calm, honest].

1.8 Account setup checklistUsed: Oct 24, 14:09 and Oct 25

Give me a checklist for setting up [Instagram, TikTok, Facebook] for a new page, including a dedicated email, handle consistency, and the first posts.

2. Strategy (Oct 25 to 27)

2.1 Content pillarsUsed: Oct 24 and Oct 25, 18:43

My page is about [mission]. Suggest [4] content pillars. Here is my own list: [pillars]. Refine it, rename anything that excludes people, and tell me what to be careful about in each pillar.

2.2 Content templateUsed: Oct 25, 18:59

Every carousel should follow this structure: [Define it, Understand it, Why it matters, In your day, Realization]. Turn this into a reusable six-slide template with placeholders, and show me an example.

2.3 Organic growth planUsed: Oct 25, 12:47

I want to grow [page] organically on [platform]. Give me a plan covering posting rhythm, formats, daily engagement, and what not to do. Assume I have [time] per day and no budget.

2.4 Audience and platform researchUsed: Oct 26 and Oct 27

Search for current data on social media use among [audience] in [country]: which platforms, how much time, and what formats. Tell me which sources you used, how recent they are, and what they can and can’t tell me.

2.5 FunnelUsed: Oct 26, 18:06

Design a simple funnel for a page with no products. I want to entertain a wide audience, educate the interested, and invite the committed, without selling. Suggest a percentage split and what each stage looks like.

2.6 Hashtag ruleUsed: Oct 26, 10:25

Check the current hashtag limit for [platform]. Then give me one brand tag plus a set of topic tags for each of my pillars: [pillars].

2.7 Trend ruleUsed: Oct 26, 12:21 to 12:22

How should I use trends without losing my page’s identity? Suggest a rule of thumb and examples of trends that suit a [calm, philosophical] page.

2.8 Weekly rhythmUsed: Oct 27 to 28 (approx.)

Plan a weekly schedule: [carousels on Sun, Tue, Thu], [photo quotes in between], and [a Saturday summary]. Show how each post connects to the one before and after it.

2.9 Topic pipelineUsed: Oct 28 (approx.)

Map the words and topics connected to [conditioning, growth, self-awareness] into a sequence I can teach in order. Group them into stages and show what each stage leads to.

3. Content production

3.1 Carousel from the templateUsed: Oct 25 onward

Using my six-slide template, make a carousel on [topic] for the pillar [pillar]. Cover hook: a question aimed at the reader. Include a [metaphor from the sea or sky]. In your day: [school or work, family or friends, online]. End with: [closing line]. Size: [1080 × 1350].

3.2 Photo quoteUsed: Oct 26 onward

Make a photo quote with the line [quote], using [photo]. Keep the text in the sky area at the top, one word in peach italic ([word]), and the page name and handle at the bottom. Size: [1080 × 1350]. Write a caption that teases [next post] and ends with [closing line], plus five hashtags.

3.3 Weekly summaryUsed: Oct 26 and each Saturday

Make a six-slide summary of this week’s posts: [topics]. Include one takeaway for each, three small steps to try, and a teaser for next week: [topics].

3.4 Captions by weekly contextUsed: Oct 26, 16:32

Write captions for these posts: [list]. Each should match the week’s theme, avoid ending with a comment question, and finish with [closing line]. Add five hashtags: [brand tag] plus four for the pillar.

3.5 Cover color rotation

Rotate cover colors through [navy, sky, cream, ocean] so two carousels in a row never open on the same color. Tell me which color the next one should use.

3.6 Story realizationsUsed: Nov 2026

Make [8] story-sized (1080 × 1920) quote images with short realizations in my page’s voice. Use a different photo for each, keep text away from the top and bottom of the screen, and highlight one word. Themes: [rest, boundaries, values].

3.7 Fix a design problemUsed: Oct 25 onward

The cover text is too close to the edge and gets cropped in the grid. Redo [post] with safer margins, and keep everything else the same.

4. Research and sources

4.1 Research templateUsed: Oct 25, 15:21

Create a template for researching [audience, competitors, thinkers, sensitive topics, sources, support lines]. Make it something I can fill in over time.

4.2 Thinker profileUsed: Oct 25, 15:07

Write a short profile of [thinker]: key ideas, one idea that suits [pillar], what to be careful about, and where I can read the original.

4.3 Check a claim

Is this claim supported: [claim]? Find the original source, say what it actually shows, and tell me how to word it so I don’t overstate it.

4.4 Support linesUsed: Oct 26 to 27

Find crisis and support lines in [country], with their numbers. Tell me which come from official sources and which from news or directories, so I know what to verify.

5. Video and Reels

5.1 Reel from a raw clipUsed: Oct 27

I’m uploading a raw clip of [scene]. Turn it into a vertical Reel for my [topic] script. Add text overlays that match each line, a navy tint for readability, and an end card with my logo and [closing line].

5.2 Voiceover mixUsed: Oct 27

Here is my voice recording. Mute the original sound, mix my voice in, and retime the on-screen text to match my pauses. Don’t add music.

5.3 Judge my videoUsed: Oct 28 to 29

Judge this video for framing, lighting, audio, background, and hook. Say what works, what to fix, and how to improve the next take. Here is the transcript: [text].

5.4 Video quoteUsed: Nov 5 to 6

Turn this raw clip into a 10-second video quote with the line [quote]. Brand fonts and colors, a navy tint, the logo end card, and the page name and handle near the bottom.

5.5 Font checkUsed: Nov 5

Which font should I use for video quotes on busy footage? Give me my brand font, a fallback, and exact text settings.

6. Analytics and testing

6.1 Read my analyticsUsed: Oct 28 to Nov 4

Here are my analytics screenshots: [attach]. What do they tell me, what don’t they tell me, and what should I test next? Keep claims modest, since my sample is small.

6.2 Posting-time testUsed: Nov 2026

I noticed more views when I post at [time]. Design a fair test over [8 to 10] posts, and tell me what to log.

6.3 Format testUsed: Nov 2026

I’m thinking of changing [photo quotes] into [video quotes]. What are the risks, and how can I test one before switching?

7. Operations

7.1 Notion databaseUsed: Oct 28 and after

Design a Notion database for [posts]. List the properties, the views to add, and give me a CSV I can import. I’m a beginner, so keep the setup steps short.

7.2 Task and project tracker

Turn everything we’ve done and still need to do into a task list with projects, status, priority, due date, and owner, as a CSV for Notion.

7.3 Web app version

Code the project management system as a web page I can use. Include a dashboard, a pipeline board, a task list, and a sources tab. Save my changes.

7.4 SOP

Write an SOP for how I run [page]. Include the weekly rhythm, build steps, caption rules, source rules, posting steps, tracking, and a monthly review. Add document control and a revision history.

7.5 Development log

Write a dated log of this page from the first brainstorm to today: naming, decisions, platforms, research, and every post. Note which dates are exact and which are approximate.

7.6 Strategy brief

Write a short brief explaining why the page works the way it does, with a table of the research behind it and what each source can and can’t support.

7.7 Brand kit

Make the page’s brand kit as a PDF: story, logo, colors with contrast ratios, typography, formats, imagery, voice, layout rules, and a quick reference page.

7.8 Workflow graphic

Make an image of how the page is managed, from planning to review, with who does each step and what has to be true before moving on. Size it for a dashboard.

8. Quick-fix prompts

NamePrompt
ShortenCut this to [number] words and keep the main idea.
Fix the voiceRewrite this in a calm, plain, honest voice. No hype.
Make a version for [platform]Adapt this post for [TikTok], keeping the hook in the first line.
Different captionWrite [3] different captions for this post with different openings.
Check before postingCheck this post against my SOP: sources, hashtags, closing line, and edges.

9. Guardrails to add to any prompt

TopicAdd this
SourcesCite sources for any research claim, and say what the source can’t tell us.
Mental healthDescribe signs only. Do not diagnose. Add a line suggesting a doctor or counselor.
PhilippinesUse Philippines-specific sources for gender, legal, and health topics.
PrivacyDon’t include faces, addresses, or details that could identify me or connect my personal accounts to this page.
QuotesOnly use quotes whose origin is clear. Otherwise write an original line.

Working with me

What to expect from first message to final files, so nothing is a surprise.

My process

  1. Inquiry. You tell me what you’re building and what you need. I reply within one business day.
  2. Scope and quote. I recommend a package and confirm in writing what’s included, the timeline and the price.
  3. Agreement and deposit. Once you approve, I send a short agreement and an invoice for a 50% deposit. Work starts when the deposit arrives.
  4. Intake. You fill in a short questionnaire about your brand, audience, goals, tone, examples you like and anything I need access to.
  5. Sample. Once the deposit and questionnaire are in, I send a sample of the work so you can see the direction.
  6. Decision. If you’d like to proceed, the remaining balance is due and I continue with the full project.
  7. Kickoff and milestones. I share a project page and break the work into milestones, so you see progress early.
  8. Draft and review. You receive the first draft and send feedback. Up to two revision rounds are included.
  9. Final delivery. You get the final files and a short guide on how to use them.

What I need from you

  • One point of contact who can give feedback and approvals.
  • A short description of your idea, brand or page, and who it’s for.
  • Any existing materials: logo, colors, past posts, notes or documents.
  • Access to shared documents or tools through their own sharing settings. I never need your passwords.
  • Feedback within two to three business days, which keeps the timeline on track.

Turnaround and availability

Most projects take between one week and one month, depending on the package and how quickly feedback comes back. I confirm the timeline in your quote before work starts.

I’m available from 5 AM to 9 PM Philippine Standard Time (UTC+8), and I reply within one business day.

Payment

I accept PayPal or bank transfer, and I can quote in Philippine pesos or US dollars. I ask for a 50% deposit to start. After you’ve seen the sample, if you decide to proceed, the remaining balance is due and I continue with the full project. If you decide not to proceed after seeing the sample, the deposit is refunded minus a sample fee, which is stated in your quote before work starts.

Communication

Email is our official channel for scope, approvals and files: quelene.santiago.wrk@gmail.com. I also set up a shared Notion project page, so you can see progress, leave feedback and approve drafts in one place. For quick questions, we can use a chat app you already use.

Revisions

Two revision rounds are included in every package. If the result still isn’t right after that, I won’t keep guessing. We’ll talk through what’s missing, I’ll ask for more information and your preferences, and then I’ll rework it. Any change to the scope is confirmed in writing before I continue.

Onboarding and welcome packet

When you say yes, you receive a welcome packet. The full packet is shared with each client privately, because it includes payment details and intake questions. Here is what’s inside:

  • A welcome note and an overview of how we’ll work together
  • Your timeline and milestones
  • The intake questionnaire: brand, audience, goals, tone, references and access
  • A guide to giving feedback and approving drafts
  • Payment details and your invoice
  • Communication channels, working hours and response time

Frequently asked questions

How do I know which package I need?

Message me what you’re building and where you’re stuck. I’ll recommend a starting point and send a quote.

Do you use AI?

Yes. I use AI for drafting and visuals, then direct, fact-check and approve everything myself. I’ll tell you where AI was used.

Do you post or manage my accounts?

No. My packages cover brand foundations, content, research and systems. Posting and day-to-day account management aren’t included.

How long will it take?

Between one week and one month, depending on the package. Your quote has the exact timeline.

How do I pay?

By PayPal or bank transfer: a 50% deposit to start, then the remaining balance after you’ve seen the sample and decide to proceed.

What is the sample?

After the deposit and intake, I send a sample of the work so you can see the direction before you commit to the full project.

What if I don’t want to proceed after the sample?

The deposit is refunded minus a sample fee, which is stated in your quote before work starts.

What if I need changes after the revisions?

We’ll talk it through, and I’ll ask for the details and preferences I need to get it right.

Work

My own project, built and run by me. Drafts and visuals are AI-assisted. I direct, fact-check and approve everything.

In Progress and Free

A calm, honest page on philosophy, feminism and freedom of mind for teens and young adults in the Philippines. I built it from the name and pillars to the weekly posting workflow.

  • Four content pillars: Philosophy of Self, Feminism for Everyone, Fragile but Growing, Actionable Awareness
  • An original framework: Notice. Question. Choose.
  • A weekly rhythm of three carousels, three quotes and a Saturday summary
  • A seven-stage workflow with a check at each stage, documented in a Content SOP and research template

Content set: Week 1, Becoming

A week of ready-to-post content for In Progress and Free, October 25 to 27, 2026, for Instagram, TikTok and Facebook. It introduces the page, conditioning, and non-linear growth.

  • 12 pieces in the set
  • 5 carousels
  • 1 Reel and 1 photo quote
  • 2 pillars, plus welcome and safety

Pieces shown: Welcome, Empowerment, Conditioning, Growth (a tree, not a ladder), Unfinished and free, Weekly prompt, Week 1 summary, Start Here, and the Growth Reel.

See the content set package

Notion content system: page manager dashboard

Five linked databases, one place to plan, build, post, and learn. This is a sample layout of the dashboard I built for In Progress and Free, using real entries from the page’s workflow.

  • Content pipeline: a board grouped by stage, from idea to posted
  • This week: a calendar of the week’s posts
  • Tasks: a list filtered to what’s not done, sorted by due date
  • Sources: every source, where it’s used, and whether it’s verified
  • Projects: progress calculated from linked tasks
  • Weekly review: top post and what to change
